tier_guide.daily: Update every trading day — spot prices, spreads
tier_guide.weekly: Update weekly — price consensus, regulatory signals, stories
tier_guide.structural: Update on major regulatory decision or market structure change

instruments.name: EU Allowances
instruments.description: European Union Emissions Trading System allowances. Each permit covers one tonne of CO2. The world's largest carbon market.
instruments.regulatory_note: Market Stability Reserve review ongoing. Outcome expected Q3 2026.

story.beginner: EU carbon allowances (EUAs) have fallen sharply, dropping nearly 9% in just one week and losing almost a quarter of their value over three months. This means it is becoming cheaper for companies to buy permission to emit carbon dioxide in Europe, which typically happens when markets worry about lower industrial activity or oversupply.
story.moderate: EUA prices have contracted significantly across all timeframes, with the steepest decline (23.7%) occurring over three months, signalling bearish sentiment on near-term compliance demand. The weakness reflects softer economic outlook expectations and potential supply concerns ahead of the Market Stability Reserve (MSR) review due in Q3 2026, which could alter the mechanics of how allowances are released into the market. Current pricing at 62.67 EUR/tonne sits at multi-month lows, testing support levels that may trigger tactical positioning shifts.
story.expert: EUAs have sold off sharply, down 23.7% over three months despite an unambiguously bullish structural backdrop, suggesting the market is pricing macro headwinds and near-term demand softness over the tightening supply trajectory. The 4.3% Linear Reduction Factor is mechanically reducing the cap, CBAM's financial phase is live with free allocation erosion beginning at 2.5% this year, and maritime's 100% compliance phase-in is adding roughly 30% incremental demand to that surrender tranche versus 2025. Yet prices continue to slide, indicating that industrial output weakness and speculative deleveraging are dominating sentiment. The April surrender deadline for 2025 emissions offers a near-term catalyst; any shortfall between verified emissions and outstanding positions will force spot buying and could arrest the decline. Beyond that, the Market Stability Reserve review outcome in Q3 will determine whether intake thresholds adjust to reflect the new supply-demand balance. Monitor EU registry data closely through April, and watch stakeholder submissions ahead of the 4 May consultation close for signals on post-2030 scope expansion.

instruments.name: California Carbon Allowances
instruments.description: California Cap-and-Trade allowances under the CARB program. Covers ~85% of California GHG emissions.
instruments.regulatory_note: 2026 cap adjustment under CARB review. Floor price mechanism provides downside support.

story.beginner: California Carbon Allowances (CCAs) are permits that allow companies to emit one tonne of greenhouse gas. They're currently trading at $28.32 per tonne, down 1.5% over the past week and month. The price has stayed relatively stable because California's rules include a price floor that prevents them from falling too far.
story.moderate: CCAs have declined 1.5% over one week and one month, holding above the regulatory floor price of $20 per tonne, which provides a mechanical support level in the California cap-and-trade system. The modest downward pressure reflects uncertainty around the 2026 cap adjustment currently under California Air Resources Board (CARB) review, which will reset the total allowances available for the next compliance period. With regulatory signals cloudy, the market is likely pricing in cautious sentiment ahead of clarity on stringency and supply allocation.
story.expert: California Carbon Allowances have drifted lower across all measured timeframes, with the 1.5% decline over the past week, month, and quarter suggesting persistent but contained bearish pressure rather than acute selling. At $28.32 per tonne, CCAs remain well above the 2026 auction reserve floor of approximately $20.72, providing meaningful structural downside support through CARB's price containment mechanism. The sideways price action reflects mixed regulatory signals as CARB reviews the 2026 cap adjustment, creating near term uncertainty around allowance supply stringency. Looking further out, the post-2030 rulemaking process expected to conclude in approximately 93 days carries bullish implications; the cap trajectory and potential tightening measures for the programme extension to 2045 will materially shape long term scarcity dynamics. Compliance entities and speculators should monitor CARB workshop outputs and any preliminary cap decline factor proposals, as these will determine whether the current price compression reverses or extends into Q3.

instruments.name: UK Allowances
instruments.description: UK Emissions Trading Scheme allowances. Launched in 2021 post-Brexit as a standalone system.
instruments.regulatory_note: UK-EU ETS linking feasibility study due 2026. Outcome would significantly affect pricing.

story.beginner: UK Allowances (UKA) are tradeable permits that allow companies to emit carbon dioxide in the UK. The price has fallen to 34.55 GBP per tonne this week, down 2.7% from last week and 15.5% over three months, suggesting weakening demand or oversupply in the market.
story.moderate: UK Allowances have declined 5.9% over the month and 15.5% over three months, reaching 34.55 GBP/tonne, reflecting softer sentiment in the compliance segment. The downward pressure may reflect expectations around the EU-UK ETS linking feasibility study due in 2026, which could restructure the market significantly. Until clarity emerges on linkage terms, price discovery remains uncertain and participants are likely adopting cautious positioning.
story.expert: UKA has shed 15.5% over three months to settle at 34.55 GBP/tonne, with the discount to EUA now stretching to historically wide levels despite a structurally bullish regulatory calendar. The imminent Auction Reserve Price increase from £22 to £28, effective in nine days, establishes a materially higher hard floor with annual GDP Deflator indexation from 2027, yet price action suggests the market is looking through near-term support mechanisms toward unresolved linking uncertainty. The UK-EU ETS feasibility study due mid-year remains the pivotal catalyst; a positive outcome would imply convergence toward EUA levels, while prolonged ambiguity keeps the discount entrenched. Maritime expansion launching in 93 days adds incremental demand, though double-surrender deferrals mute immediate impact. CBAM implementation in 277 days provides a structural demand anchor that limits downside scenarios on a 12-month horizon. Watch feasibility study language closely; any signal of accelerated negotiation timelines or mutual recognition frameworks would justify rapid repricing of the current UKA-EUA spread.

instruments.name: CORSIA Credits
instruments.description: Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation. ICAO-governed global mechanism requiring airlines to offset emissions growth above 2019 baseline.
instruments.regulatory_note: Phase 1 demand growing as aviation recovers. Eligible fuels criteria update expected mid-2026.

story.beginner: CORSIA credits cost around 6.40 dollars per tonne. Airlines must buy these credits to offset the growth in their CO2 emissions above 2019 levels. As air travel keeps recovering from COVID lows, airlines need more credits, pushing prices higher.
story.moderate: CORSIA credits at 6.40 USD/tonne have risen 12% over three months as aviation demand recovery drives offsetting obligations higher. Phase 1 (2024-2026) covers voluntary participants, with Phase 2 (2027+) becoming mandatory. The eligible fuels criteria update mid-2026 is worth watching: if ICAO broadens the list of qualifying credits, supply could increase and cap price appreciation. Supply is currently constrained by the narrow list of CORSIA-eligible credit types.
story.expert: CORSIA credits have extended their rally with a 12.3% gain over three months, driven by firming Phase 1 compliance demand as international aviation volumes recover toward pre-pandemic levels. The current $6.40/tonne price reflects a market still digesting the implications of ICAO's ongoing eligible emissions unit standards review; any tightening of quality criteria would compress eligible supply against growing airline offset obligations under the 93-state mandatory phase running through 2026. The EU's CORSIA assessment decision in approximately 93 days represents the most material near-term binary risk, as a negative finding could trigger ETS extension to extra-European departures, fragmenting demand signals across the two regimes. The Phase 1 to Phase 2 transition at year-end introduces additional uncertainty around baseline recalculation and unit eligibility, with supply constraints in CORSIA-compliant credits already becoming apparent. Traders should monitor mid-2026 eligible fuels criteria updates and COP31 progress on Article 6.4 supervisory body rulebook finalisation, which will determine whether A6.4ERs can scale into CORSIA eligibility in time to relieve anticipated supply tightness.

instruments.name: California LCFS Credits
instruments.description: Low Carbon Fuel Standard credits generated by producing or blending fuels below California's carbon intensity benchmark.
instruments.regulatory_note: Prices under pressure. CARB 2030 pathway consultation could reset the carbon intensity benchmark and restore credit value.

story.beginner: California LCFS credits, which reward cleaner fuels, have fallen to $57 per credit as the market faces uncertainty. The state is consulting on new rules that could change how credits are valued, so traders are holding back until they know what's coming.
story.moderate: LCFS credits have declined 1.7% over one week, one month, and three months, suggesting sustained selling pressure as market participants await CARB's 2030 pathway consultation. The regulatory signal is stormy: any material reset to the carbon intensity benchmark could alter credit generation rates and scarcity dynamics. Current weakness reflects hesitation ahead of potential rule changes that may either restore or further compress credit values.
story.expert: LCFS credits remain under pressure at $57, down 1.7% across all recent timeframes, reflecting persistent oversupply despite the structural tightening now in effect. The July 2025 amendments delivered a 9% step-change in the carbon intensity benchmark, successfully flipping the credit bank from net surplus to net deficit by Q3 2025; however, the accumulated surplus continues to weigh on spot prices as the market digests years of credit overhang. The first full compliance year under the amended regulation will be critical, as the pace of credit bank erosion through 2026 will determine whether CARB's Auto-Acceleration Mechanism triggers in 2027, which would introduce additional tightening catalysts. Current price weakness appears disconnected from the improving structural fundamentals, suggesting either delayed price discovery or market skepticism about enforcement stringency. Traders should monitor quarterly credit bank data and deficit generation rates closely, as confirmation of accelerating drawdown could catalyze a repricing toward levels more consistent with the tightened pathway.

instruments.name: Renewable Fuel Standard Credits
instruments.description: Renewable Identification Numbers under the EPA Renewable Fuel Standard. D3 (cellulosic) and D6 (conventional ethanol) are the benchmark categories.
instruments.regulatory_note: EPA 2026 volume obligations final rule pending. Obligated parties watching for RVO levels.

story.beginner: RINs are credits that oil refiners must buy to prove they have blended enough renewable fuel into petrol and diesel. The D6 benchmark currently trades at around 68 cents. When the EPA sets higher blending requirements, refiners need more RINs and prices rise.
story.moderate: D6 RINs at 0.68 USD are range-bound ahead of the EPA's 2026 Renewable Volume Obligation final rule. The RVO level is the primary price driver: a higher obligation requires refiners to surrender more RINs, tightening supply and pushing prices up. D3 (cellulosic) RINs command a significant premium at approximately 2.80 USD, reflecting scarcer supply from advanced biofuel producers. Small refinery exemptions remain a wildcard: if the EPA grants more exemptions, effective demand for RINs falls.
story.expert: D6 RINs have firmed modestly over the past month, gaining 3.0% to $0.68, as the market positions ahead of EPA's imminent 2026 to 2028 Renewable Volume Obligation rulemaking expected within days. The near-term price recovery reflects speculative demand from obligated parties hedging against potentially higher conventional biofuel blending mandates, though the 4.2% decline over three months signals persistent structural uncertainty around the administration's biofuel policy posture. The regulatory signal remains mixed; while the RVO rulemaking is directionally bullish for RIN demand, final volume levels remain unpublished, leaving compliance buyers cautious about building long positions. Separately, the interplay with IRS 45Z clean fuel production credits adds complexity, as interim lifecycle methodology guidance continues to influence producer economics and, by extension, RIN generation incentives. Market participants should monitor the EPA final rule release for specific gallon-equivalent mandates across D3 through D6 categories, as any upward revision to conventional ethanol obligations would provide immediate price support, while a status quo outcome could trigger renewed selling pressure.

instruments.name: 45Z Clean Fuel Credits
instruments.description: IRA-created production tax credit for clean transportation fuels. Replaces the Blenders Tax Credit from 2025. Value depends on the carbon intensity of the fuel produced.
instruments.regulatory_note: IRS guidance finalisation pending. High uncertainty around credit calculation methodology and eligible fuel types.

story.beginner: The 45Z credit is a new US government incentive that pays fuel producers for making cleaner transportation fuels. The cleaner the fuel, the larger the credit. It is still new and the exact rules are not fully finalised, creating uncertainty for fuel producers planning investments.
story.moderate: 45Z replaced the Blenders Tax Credit in 2025 and is structured as a production credit rather than a blending credit, shifting the incentive from blenders to producers. The credit value is inversely linked to carbon intensity: fuels below 50g CO2e per MJ qualify, with higher credits for lower-CI fuels. IRS guidance finalisation is the critical near-term event. Uncertainty around the GREET model update and international feedstock eligibility has delayed investment decisions across the sustainable aviation fuel and renewable diesel sectors.
story.expert: The 45Z Clean Fuel Production Credit remains structurally untradeable in any standardized form, with credit values entirely dependent on fuel-specific carbon intensity scores that lack final IRS methodology guidance. The credit, which replaced the Blenders Tax Credit beginning in 2025, offers up to $1.00 per gallon for clean transportation fuels and $1.75 per gallon for sustainable aviation fuel, but actual values scale linearly based on lifecycle emissions relative to petroleum baselines. Market participants face significant uncertainty as the IRS has issued only interim guidance on lifecycle analysis methodology, leaving producers unable to definitively calculate credit eligibility or value for key pathways including renewable diesel, SAF, and hydrogen-derived fuels. The regulatory signal is decidedly bearish given this methodological limbo, which constrains project financing and offtake structuring across the clean fuels sector. Watch for final IRS rulemaking on GREET model adoption and pathway-specific carbon intensity thresholds, as these determinations will immediately establish the credit's effective price architecture and unlock deferred production decisions.

instruments.name: Voluntary Carbon Credits
instruments.description: Nature-based voluntary carbon credits verified under Verra VCS or Gold Standard. REDD+, reforestation, and soil carbon project types. Prices vary by vintage, project type, and co-benefits.
instruments.regulatory_note: Verra VM0042 REDD+ methodology update active. Article 6 bilateral agreements could redirect supply toward compliance markets.

story.beginner: Voluntary carbon credits are environmental certificates that companies buy to offset their emissions outside of government regulations. The price of nature-based credits has risen 2.5% over the past week, month, and three months, suggesting modest buyer demand as climate commitments remain in focus.
story.moderate: Nature-based voluntary carbon credits (VCM) have appreciated 2.5% across all measured timeframes, settling at USD 6.5/tonne. The steady gains reflect stable demand from corporate net-zero commitments, though the regulatory environment remains uncertain. Verra's updated REDD+ methodology and potential Article 6 bilateral agreements could shift supply allocation toward compliance markets, which may tighten voluntary supply pools if governments prioritise international emissions trading.
story.expert: Voluntary carbon credits have posted a modest 2.5% gain over the past quarter, stabilizing near $6.50/tonne as the market digests ongoing integrity concerns surrounding nature-based methodologies. The Verra VM0042 REDD+ methodology update remains the dominant structural overhang; while revisions aim to restore credibility following the 2023 additionality controversies, buyers continue to apply steep discounts to legacy vintages and unverified project types. Article 6 bilateral agreements present a medium-term supply risk, as host countries increasingly channel high-quality removals toward sovereign compliance obligations rather than voluntary retirement. The regulatory signal remains mixed, with CORSIA's eligible emissions unit standards review potentially tightening quality thresholds, which would squeeze supply for aviation-grade credits while further segmenting the broader VCM. COP31 in Belém represents the critical inflection point; progress on Article 6.4 rulebook finalisation and whether A6.4ERs achieve scale issuance will determine whether compliance demand cannibalizes premium voluntary supply or creates a two-tier market structure.

events.title: EU ETS Phase 4 Linear Reduction Factor increase
events.summary: The EU ETS Linear Reduction Factor increased from 2.2% to 4.3% from 2024 onwards (rising to 4.4% in 2028). This accelerates the annual decline in the cap and is the primary long-run structural support for EUA prices.
events.analyst_note: The LRF increase from 2.2% to 4.3% is already law and in effect. The structural case for EUA is intact: the cap tightens faster, fewer allowances exist each year, and covered sectors have limited short-run abatement options. This is the floor beneath any bullish EUA thesis.

scenarios.rationale: The accelerated linear reduction factor to 4.3% appears likely to provide underlying support for EUA prices, though market dynamics and abatement responses could moderate the impact.
Structural supply constraints from the higher LRF could drive more pronounced price appreciation if industrial demand remains resilient and abatement options prove limited in the near term.
Weaker industrial activity and accelerated technological adoption might offset the tighter supply trajectory, particularly if economic headwinds reduce emissions demand.

events.title: CARB LCFS re-adoption and 2030 CI benchmark tightening
events.summary: CARB re-adopted the LCFS in 2024 with tighter carbon intensity benchmarks through 2030 designed to restore credit value following structural oversupply from EV charging credits. New pathways and reporting requirements also introduced. Bullish for LCFS credit prices.
events.analyst_note: This is already in effect. The 2024 amendments took full effect July 2025 with a 9% step-change in CI benchmark, turning the credit bank from net surplus to net deficit in Q3 2025. CARB projects credit prices recovering toward $100 to $200 per credit. The structural oversupply that depressed prices since 2022 is unwinding. The re-adoption is the single most important near-term driver of LCFS price recovery.
events.source_label: CARB, Low Carbon Fuel Standard Regulation Amendment, Board approved 8 November 2024; OAL effective July 2025

scenarios.rationale: The 2024 amendments have taken effect and the 9% CI benchmark step-change in July 2025 likely achieves CARB's intention of transitioning from credit surplus to deficit, though sustained price recovery to projected £100-200 range may face headwinds from remaining credit bank and market uncertainties.

Strong demand response materialises quickly with tighter CI benchmarks and automatic adjustment mechanism triggers creating additional supply constraints, whilst limited RD import capacity and EV charging credit moderation accelerate credit bank draw-down beyond CARB projections.

Implementation delays, legal challenges, or federal policy changes could undermine the amendments' effectiveness, whilst continued oversupply from remaining credit inventory and slower-than-expected obligated party compliance responses may limit price recovery despite the tighter benchmarks.

events.title: IRS 45Z clean fuel production credit guidance
events.summary: The 45Z credit became effective January 2025 replacing the biodiesel tax credit. IRS issued interim guidance on lifecycle methodology (GREET-based). Final guidance on feedstock-specific pathways and sustainable aviation fuel definitions is pending and will determine credit values for key fuel types.
events.analyst_note: The 45Z credit is live but the lifecycle methodology guidance for key fuel pathways, including sustainable aviation fuel and hydrogen, remains interim. Final IRS guidance will determine which feedstocks qualify at which credit values. Uncertainty is currently depressing investment in some pathways. Resolution is bullish for producers with qualifying fuels. Confidence is High on the credit existing; Medium on the specific pathway values.
events.source_label: IRS/Treasury, Notice 2025-10 and Notice 2025-11, Section 45Z Clean Fuel Production Credit Guidance, 10 January 2025

scenarios.rationale: The IRS appears likely to publish comprehensive proposed regulations in Q1-Q2 2026, providing substantial clarity on feedstock pathways and emissions methodologies whilst resolving most outstanding uncertainties around provisional emissions rates and qualifying sale definitions.

Final regulations may be published ahead of schedule with particularly favourable provisions for feedstock-specific pathways and Climate Smart Agriculture practices, potentially delivering significantly higher credit values than initially anticipated.

The Trump Administration's regulatory freeze and potential policy reversals could significantly delay final guidance publication beyond May 2026, prolonging investment uncertainty and market volatility.

events.title: CBAM definitive phase launch
events.summary: The Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism moves from transitional reporting to full financial adjustment in January 2026. Importers of cement, steel, aluminium, fertilisers, electricity, and hydrogen must purchase CBAM certificates. Free allocation for covered sectors begins phasing out in parallel.
events.analyst_note: CBAM is live in its financial phase from January 2026, but the free allocation phase-out for covered sectors is gradual (2.5% reduction in 2026). Near-term impact on EUA demand is limited. The structural bullish read is for 2028 and beyond, when free allocation reductions accelerate and CBAM certificate demand builds. For now it is more signal than substance.
events.source_label: European Parliament & Council, Regulation (EU) 2023/956 establishing CBAM, 10 May 2023

scenarios.rationale: The CBAM's financial implementation from January 2026 may provide modest structural support to EUA prices, though near-term demand impacts remain limited due to the gradual 2.5% reduction in free allocations.

Rising expectations for expanded CBAM coverage and accelerated free allocation phase-outs could drive stronger anticipatory EUA demand from both European industry and foreign producers hedging future compliance costs.
Implementation challenges, delayed certificate purchasing until February 2027, or weaker-than-expected import volumes might limit CBAM's immediate influence on carbon market dynamics.

events.title: EU ETS maritime 100% compliance phase-in
events.summary: From 1 January 2026 shipping companies must surrender EUAs for 100% of verified CO2, up from 70% in 2025. The phase-in is complete. New demand from ~5,000 GT vessels now fully priced into the cap.
events.analyst_note: Effective demand increase of ~30% on the maritime surrender tranche vs 2025. Watch verified emissions data vs allowances surrendered — any shortfall triggers cancellation from the auction calendar.

scenarios.rationale: Maritime demand increase likely proceeds smoothly, with the 30% additional allowance requirement gradually absorbed by shipping companies who have had two years to prepare for full compliance.

Strong winter demand coincides with the effective ~30% maritime demand increase, whilst any compliance shortfalls from 2024-2025 trigger additional auction volume cancellations that tighten supply further.
Maritime compliance proves less impactful than anticipated due to operational adjustments or route optimisation, whilst broader economic headwinds reduce industrial demand for allowances.

events.title: EU ETS free allocation CBAM phase-out begins
events.summary: From 2026, free allocation to CBAM-covered sectors (iron and steel, cement, aluminium, fertilisers, hydrogen) begins a gradual phase-out. The CBAM factor is 97.5% in 2026, declining to 51.5% in 2030 and 14% in 2033. This is the first year the phase-out mechanism creates a real demand signal by reducing the volume of allowances freely distributed to covered installations.
events.analyst_note: The phase-out is already law and running. The 2.5% reduction in 2026 is modest in isolation but the trajectory is steep — by 2030 nearly half of current free allocation to these sectors will have been withdrawn. Watch annual verified emissions data from CBAM sectors to gauge how quickly the net demand effect compounds.

scenarios.rationale: The 2.5% reduction in free allocation in 2026 creates a modest but measurable demand signal, though the immediate impact is likely constrained by the small initial adjustment factor.

Market participants may price in the steep trajectory ahead and the psychological significance of the phase-out beginning, creating stronger anticipatory demand pressure than the mechanics alone suggest.
The minimal 2.5% adjustment factor in 2026 may prove insufficient to generate meaningful net demand effects in the near term, particularly if industrial production remains subdued.

events.title: EU ETS 2 launch (buildings and road transport)
events.summary: A separate EU ETS covering buildings and road transport launches in 2027 with a price corridor of 45-60 EUR/tonne. Distinct from the existing EU ETS; allowances are not fungible. Creates a new compliance market but does not directly affect EUA supply-demand.
events.analyst_note: ETS2 is a separate market, not fungible with EUA. Its launch does not directly affect EUA supply or demand. We flag it as Neutral for EUA precisely because the two systems are ring-fenced. Watch for political pressure to merge or coordinate them post-2030, which would be a material structural change.
events.source_label: European Parliament & Council, Directive (EU) 2023/959, Chapter IVa (ETS2), 10 May 2023

scenarios.rationale: ETS2 operates as a separate ring-fenced system, likely generating modest market attention but limited direct EUA price effects given non-fungible allowances.
Market sentiment may moderately favour EUA if ETS2 demonstrates EU commitment to expanding carbon pricing coverage and validates the broader carbon market architecture.
Political resistance to ETS2 could potentially weaken confidence in EU carbon policy framework, creating modest headwinds for EUA despite lack of direct market linkage.

events.title: CORSIA first mandatory phase (2024-2026)
events.summary: CORSIA transitioned from its voluntary pilot phase to the first mandatory phase covering international aviation emissions growth above the 2019 baseline. 93 states participating. Demand for eligible emissions units (EEUs) will grow through 2026 as airlines accumulate obligations.
events.analyst_note: 93 states are participating. Airline obligations accrue through 2026 and must be settled with eligible emissions units. Demand is real but modest in Phase 1 given the COVID-adjusted baseline. The more important read is on Phase 2 (2027-2035) where obligations grow substantially. Phase 1 is the demand foundation; Phase 2 is the price catalyst.
events.source_label: ICAO, Annex 16 Volume IV (CORSIA SARPs) 2nd Edition, effective 1 January 2024; Assembly Resolution A41-22, October 2022

scenarios.rationale: CORSIA Phase 1 demand could reach the upper-bound of projections as participating states successfully implement compliance mechanisms, though supply constraints may limit price appreciation.
Strong airline compliance combined with continued delays in host country letters of authorisation could create significant supply shortages, driving prices well above current projections.
Lower-than-expected airline emissions growth or accelerated approval of new credit programmes could ease supply-demand tensions and moderate price increases.

events.title: UK Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism launch
events.summary: The UK government confirmed a Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism launching 1 January 2027, with enabling legislation in the Finance Bill 2025-26. Indirect emissions will not be included until 2029 at earliest.
events.analyst_note: Structural demand anchor for UKA pricing as CBAM aligns import carbon costs with the domestic ETS price. Creates medium-term ceiling on free allocation phase-down speed and supports UKA floor.

scenarios.rationale: The UK CBAM's structural demand support for UKA pricing appears likely to materialise as intended, given the mechanism's design to align import costs with domestic ETS rates.
Strong implementation effectiveness combined with delayed free allocation phase-down could create more substantial upward pressure on UKA prices than currently anticipated.
Implementation challenges or limited sectoral coverage might constrain the CBAM's ability to provide meaningful demand anchoring for UKA in the near term.

events.title: UK ETS energy-from-waste voluntary monitoring phase
events.summary: UK ETS is expanding to include energy-from-waste and incineration plants. The voluntary monitoring phase began 1 January 2026 — operators measure, report, and verify emissions to the UK ETS Authority but incur no financial liability yet. Full compliance with surrender obligations begins 1 January 2028.
events.analyst_note: New demand sector entering UK ETS from 2028. The voluntary monitoring phase now running is generating the verified emissions baseline that will determine the size of the demand increase. Watch monitoring data publications from the UK ETS Authority for early indicators of sector-wide emission volumes.

scenarios.rationale: The voluntary monitoring phase appears to be proceeding as planned whilst uncertainty remains around the scale of new demand until final emissions data is published and potential cost pass-through mechanisms are clarified.

Higher than anticipated fossil fuel emissions from the waste sector during the monitoring phase could drive substantially greater new allowance demand from 2028, particularly if cost pass-through mechanisms fail to dampen compliance obligations.

Significant waste diversion to landfill or export markets due to carbon pricing could materially reduce the expected demand increase, though this outcome appears less likely given regulatory safeguards being developed.

events.title: California CCA auction reserve price adjustment 2026
events.summary: CARB adjusts the CCA auction reserve price (floor) annually by 5% plus inflation. The 2026 floor is approximately $20.72/tonne. Provides a structural price floor that limits CCA downside and anchors the secondary market.
events.analyst_note: The CCA auction reserve price is adjusted mechanically each year: 5% plus inflation. The 2026 floor is approximately $20.72 per tonne. This is a structural feature, not an event with an uncertain outcome. Confidence is High because the formula is codified and CARB has never deviated from it. It provides a hard price floor that CCA cannot trade through in the primary market, anchoring the secondary market and limiting downside risk for holders.
events.source_label: CARB, 2026 Annual Auction Reserve Price Notice (Cap-and-Trade Regulation, Appendix C), December 2025

scenarios.rationale: The reserve price adjustment is mechanically applied and provides modest structural support, though secondary market trading may remain relatively muted given current market conditions.
The floor price increase could catalyse renewed investor interest and buying support, particularly given the substantial discount to historical highs of around $48 per tonne.
Despite the floor price increase, broader market sentiment remains weak and the adjustment may have limited impact on secondary market pricing dynamics.

events.title: UK ETS maritime expansion launch
events.summary: The UK government has confirmed 1 July 2026 as the launch date for the UK ETS maritime regime, covering domestic shipping journeys for vessels of 5,000 GT or above. A double-surrender arrangement applies for 2026-2027, with allowances due by 30 April 2028.
events.analyst_note: New demand entrants from mid-2026. Double-surrender in year one means the financial impact is deferred but certain — watch onboarding volumes for Q3 UKA auction demand signal.

scenarios.rationale: The UK ETS maritime expansion proceeds on schedule with moderate industry onboarding, likely generating steady demand for approximately 2 million UKA in the first year as maritime operators prepare for double-surrender obligations by April 2028.

Strong maritime sector participation exceeds expectations with robust pre-compliance purchasing activity, particularly as operators hedge against potential price rises and secure allowances well ahead of the 2028 surrender deadline.

Limited initial uptake occurs due to industry preparation delays or regulatory uncertainty, with maritime operators deferring allowance purchases given the extended double-surrender timeline and potential market volatility.

events.title: EU ETS post-2030 public consultation close
events.summary: The European Commission's public consultation on the post-2030 EU ETS implementation package runs from 9 February to 4 May 2026. It explores how ETS-covered emissions interact with national climate targets in the post-2030 framework.
events.analyst_note: Consultation close on 4 May is a soft catalyst — direction of stakeholder submissions informs the July proposal above. Watch for industry positions on scope expansion and removal crediting.

scenarios.rationale: Stakeholder submissions likely echo earlier consultation feedback supporting the EU ETS as an effective instrument, providing modest directional clarity for the July proposal whilst maintaining policy uncertainty around scope expansion and carbon removal integration.

Consensus emerges favouring permanent carbon removal inclusion and scope expansion, signalling potential supply tightening mechanisms and enhanced ambition for the post-2030 framework that could underpin stronger carbon pricing.

Industry submissions emphasise concerns over carbon removal integration and the 5% international credit flexibility, potentially weakening supply constraints and creating pressure for more accommodative post-2030 framework design.

events.title: UK ETS Auction Reserve Price increase £22→£28
events.summary: The UK ETS Auction Reserve Price rises from £22 to £28, taking effect for the 8 April 2026 auction, an increase of 27%. Mandated by the Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme Auctioning (Amendment) Regulations 2026.
events.analyst_note: A hard price floor rise of this magnitude is a direct bullish signal for UKA. From 2027 the ARP increases annually in line with GDP Deflator, locking in real-terms escalation.

scenarios.rationale: The 27% ARP increase from £22 to £28 establishes a stronger price floor whilst current UKA prices trade well above this level, providing modest upside support.
Market participants may interpret the substantial ARP increase and inflation-proofing mechanism as a strong policy commitment to higher carbon pricing, potentially driving increased buying interest.
The new ARP remains significantly below current trading levels around £49, limiting immediate impact whilst some participants might view the increase as already priced into forward curves.

events.title: California LCFS first full compliance year under amended regulation
events.summary: 2026 is the first full compliance year under CARB's July 2025 amended LCFS regulation. New carbon intensity benchmarks are in effect: gasoline benchmark dropped from 85.77 to 76.60 gCO2e/MJ and diesel from 86.64 to 81.70. The regulation shifts to CA-GREET 4.0 for new pathway applications. The Auto-Acceleration Mechanism can tighten targets further if the credit bank remains oversupplied, with the earliest trigger date 15 May 2027.
events.analyst_note: Tightening CI benchmarks will erode the existing credit bank over 2026. The pace of erosion determines whether the AAM triggers in 2027 — a further tightening catalyst. Watch quarterly CARB credit balance reports for bank drawdown trajectory. CA-GREET 4.0 transition affects which fuel pathways qualify for credit generation and may reduce supply from some existing projects.

scenarios.rationale: The tightened carbon intensity benchmarks will likely erode the existing credit bank through 2026, but the pace may not be sufficient to trigger the Auto-Acceleration Mechanism by May 2027.
Rapid credit bank depletion through 2026 could trigger the AAM in May 2027, creating additional tightening and further supporting credit prices.
The credit bank may prove more resilient than expected, with CA-GREET 4.0 transitions potentially creating new credit supply that moderates the tightening impact.

events.title: Article 6.4 carbon market rulebook finalisation
events.summary: Negotiations on the Paris Agreement Article 6.4 mechanism (the new international carbon market) are ongoing. COP31 (2026) is the target for finalising the supervisory body rulebook including methodology standards and corresponding adjustment requirements. Progress is bullish for high-quality VCM credits.
events.analyst_note: Article 6.4 has been in negotiation since Paris. COP31 in Brazil (November 2026) is the target for supervisory body rulebook finalisation. Progress is genuine but slow: methodology standards and corresponding adjustment requirements remain contentious. A finalised rulebook would create a new class of internationally recognised credits that could significantly expand demand for high-quality VCM projects. We see this as the long-run structural driver for premium VCM credit prices.
events.source_label: UNFCCC Article 6.4 Supervisory Body; COP29 Decision on Article 6.4 Mechanism Standards, November 2024

scenarios.rationale: Progress on Article 6.4 appears steady with first methodologies approved and the mechanism expected to become fully operational by 2026, though technical standards and registry implementation may face delays given the complex nature of remaining rulebook elements.

Complete finalisation of Article 6.4 rulebook could create significant momentum for international carbon cooperation, potentially establishing clear pathways for high-integrity VCM credits to achieve international recognition and premium pricing.

Technical disagreements over methodology standards, non-permanence requirements, or corresponding adjustments could delay full operationalisation beyond 2026, particularly given ongoing contentions around baseline setting and permanence standards.

events.title: UK ETS cap review and tightening
events.summary: The UK government is consulting on tightening the UK ETS cap trajectory post-2030 and potentially introducing a carbon price floor. A tighter cap would support UKA prices. Consultation outcome expected H1 2026.
events.analyst_note: The UK government's stated trajectory is tighter caps and a potential carbon price floor, aligned with net zero commitments. A price floor would be structurally bullish, removing UKA downside risk analogous to the CCA auction reserve price. Confidence is Medium because the consultation is ongoing and the timeline has slipped before.
events.source_label: UK ETS Authority (DESNZ), UK ETS Policy Overview; Net Zero Cap effective January 2024

scenarios.rationale: The consultation likely results in moderate cap tightening for post-2030 with inflation-linked auction reserve price increases but potentially delays the carbon price floor implementation whilst maintaining net-zero trajectory commitments.

The government implements both aggressive cap tightening and introduces a carbon price floor mechanism by H1 2026, providing structural price support similar to the current auction reserve price but at elevated levels.

Political pressures or economic concerns lead to consultation delays beyond H1 2026 or result in more modest cap adjustments than currently anticipated, undermining market confidence in policy trajectory tightening.

events.title: CORSIA eligible emissions unit standards review
events.summary: ICAO is reviewing which voluntary carbon standards produce credits eligible as CORSIA EEUs. Any expansion of approved standards increases supply (bearish); tightening of quality criteria reduces supply (bullish). Review outcome expected H1 2026.
events.analyst_note: ICAO's review of approved standards is ongoing. Any tightening of quality criteria would reduce eligible supply and lift EEU prices. Any expansion of approved programmes increases supply. We read the direction of travel as toward tighter quality criteria given broader VCM credibility pressures, but the timeline and scope are uncertain. Bullish read is conditional on a tightening outcome.
events.source_label: ICAO Council, CORSIA Eligible Emissions Units Document (updated October 2025); TAB 2024 assessment cycle

scenarios.rationale: ICAO likely tightens some quality criteria whilst maintaining current approved standards, following ongoing credibility pressures in the voluntary carbon market.
Significant tightening of eligibility criteria removes substantial supply from current approved programmes, driven by heightened scrutiny over double-counting and additionality.
ICAO expands approved standards or relaxes criteria to ensure adequate supply for growing aviation offsetting requirements, prioritising liquidity over stringency.

events.title: Verra VCS methodology review for REDD+ credits
events.summary: Verra is revising REDD+ (avoided deforestation) methodologies following credibility challenges in 2023. Revised VM0007 and related standards expected H1 2026. Tighter additionality and leakage requirements are likely to reduce issuance volumes and may require re-verification of existing projects.
events.analyst_note: The 2023 investigative reporting on REDD+ additionality failures triggered a significant credibility crisis for nature-based VCM credits. Verra's revised VM0007 and related standards are expected to materially tighten additionality and leakage requirements. This is bearish for issuance volumes of existing REDD+ projects and likely to require re-verification. It is ultimately bullish for the long-run credibility of the VCM, but the near-term impact is supply contraction and price pressure on lower-quality credits.
events.source_label: Verra, VM0048 Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation (VCS Program), launched 27 November 2023

scenarios.rationale: Verra's new VM0048 methodology appears to be a significant improvement over previous baseline-setting approaches, though it could potentially initiate supply contraction through tighter requirements for existing REDD+ projects.
The new methodology may ultimately strengthen market confidence and reduce conflicts of interest, though implementation could be less disruptive than anticipated.
Widespread re-verification requirements and retroactive application of tighter additionality standards could trigger significant market disruption alongside continued integrity concerns.

events.title: UK-EU ETS linking feasibility study
events.summary: The UK and EU committed to a feasibility study on linking the UK ETS and EU ETS
events.analyst_note: The political will exists on both sides but the governance complexity is real: cap-setting, mutual recognition, and regulatory alignment are all contested. A positive feasibility outcome would converge UKA and EUA prices, likely lifting UKA which currently trades at a discount. We rate confidence Medium because a feasibility study outcome is not a linking deal, and actual linking requires further legislation.
events.source_label: UK-EU Summit, Common Understanding on a Renewed Agenda for Cooperation (ETS linkage, Chapter IV), 19 May 2025

scenarios.rationale: The feasibility study likely yields a positive outcome given stated political will, though governance complexity around cap-setting and regulatory alignment may necessitate extended negotiation timeframes beyond initial estimates.

A comprehensive positive feasibility assessment coupled with accelerated legislative progress could drive significant convergence towards EUA pricing, particularly given the substantial discount UKA currently trades at relative to EUA.

The feasibility study may highlight irreconcilable governance differences or political obstacles that dampen near-term linking prospects, though outright rejection appears unlikely given mutual CBAM avoidance incentives.

events.title: CARB Cap-and-Trade post-2030 rulemaking
events.summary: CARB is developing amendments to the Cap-and-Trade regulation for the post-2030 period, including cap trajectory, free allocation methodology, and offset credit provisions. Rulemaking expected to conclude H2 2026. Programme extension to 2045 likely; terms will determine price trajectory.
events.analyst_note: California's Cap-and-Trade programme extension to 2045 is widely expected and has broad legislative support following AB 32 and SB 32. The key variable is the post-2030 cap trajectory and free allocation treatment. More ambitious terms would be structurally bullish for CCA. We rate confidence Medium because CARB rulemaking timelines routinely slip.
events.source_label: CARB, Cap-and-Invest Program Proposed Rulemaking (AB 1207/SB 840), public comment Jan-Mar 2026

scenarios.rationale: CARB likely proceeds with rulemaking in H2 2026 delivering programme extension to 2045 with moderately ambitious cap trajectory, though recent delays and federal administration considerations may temper strictness.

Rulemaking delivers tighter-than-expected cap trajectory with meaningful allowance removals through 2030 and aggressive post-2030 trajectory, supported by legislative momentum and climate commitments despite potential implementation delays.

Rulemaking faces further delays beyond H2 2026 or delivers weaker cap terms due to affordability concerns and federal policy uncertainty, potentially disappointing market expectations for programme ambition.

events.title: EU ETS aviation stop-the-clock expiry and CORSIA assessment
events.summary: The stop-the-clock mechanism limiting EU ETS aviation scope to intra-EU flights expires at end of 2026. The European Commission is scheduled to publish a CORSIA assessment by mid-2026 to determine whether it is sufficiently aligned with the Paris Agreement. Subject to the outcome, a legislative proposal could extend EU ETS scope to departing extra-European flights.
events.analyst_note: Outcome is binary and high-impact: a negative CORSIA assessment could trigger EU ETS extension to extra-European departures, materially increasing aviation demand for EUAs. A positive assessment preserves the status quo. Commission report timing (mid-2026) is the near-term catalyst to watch.

scenarios.rationale: The European Commission could assess CORSIA as partially adequate but insufficiently ambitious, likely leading to a phased expansion of EU ETS to departing extra-European flights with limited initial scope.

A negative CORSIA assessment finding insufficient alignment with Paris Agreement goals would probably trigger full EU ETS expansion to all extra-European departures, substantially increasing aviation demand for allowances.
The Commission might evaluate CORSIA as sufficiently strengthened and globally implemented, potentially maintaining the stop-the-clock mechanism and preserving current aviation scope limitations.

events.title: EPA Renewable Volume Obligation rulemaking 2026-2028
events.summary: The EPA sets annual Renewable Volume Obligations determining how many RINs obligated parties must retire. The 2026-2028 RVO rulemaking is underway; final rule expected Q2 2026. Higher volumes are bullish for D4/D5/D6 RIN prices; Small Refinery Exemption decisions also a key variable.
events.analyst_note: EPA RVO-setting is the primary demand driver for D4, D5, and D6 RINs. Higher RVOs directly increase obligated party demand. The current administration's posture toward biofuels mandates will be the key variable. Small Refinery Exemption decisions can materially reduce effective demand even when headline RVOs are high. We flag this as the single most important near-term regulatory event for RIN prices.
events.source_label: US EPA, Proposed Rule: RFS Standards for 2026 and 2027, 90 Fed. Reg. 25786, 17 June 2025

scenarios.rationale: The final rule establishes record-high volume obligations with substantial partial reallocation of small refinery exemptions, though uncertainty remains around future SRE policy implementation.

Full reallocation of previously exempted volumes combined with strict enforcement against further small refinery exemptions could drive significant additional RIN demand beyond the final rule baseline.
Legal challenges to volume increases or unexpected administrative reversals on foreign fuel restrictions could diminish the bullish impact of the final rule on obligated party demand.

events.title: EU Market Stability Reserve review outcome
events.summary: The European Commission is reviewing MSR parameters including the intake rate (currently 24%) and cancellation threshold. Outcome expected Q3 2026. A tightening of parameters would be structurally bullish for EUA; any loosening would weigh on price.
events.analyst_note: The Commission consultation closed July 2025 and a legislative proposal is expected by July 2026. Most stakeholders and the European Parliament favour maintaining the 24% intake rate and the cancellation mechanism. A loosening is politically unlikely given the Clean Industrial Deal narrative. We read the base case as no net change to MSR tightness, with upside risk from additional cancellation provisions.
events.source_label: European Parliament & Council, Decision (EU) 2023/852 amending Decision 2015/1814 (MSR), 19 April 2023

scenarios.rationale: The Commission consultation appears likely to maintain the current 24% intake rate and cancellation mechanism through 2030, given strong stakeholder support for existing parameters.
Additional cancellation provisions or tighter thresholds could emerge from the review, potentially strengthening the MSR's structural impact on allowance supply.
Political pressure for industrial competitiveness might lead to modest parameter loosening, though this appears unlikely given Clean Industrial Deal commitments.

events.title: EU ETS post-2030 Commission revision proposal
events.summary: The 2026 Commission work programme includes a climate package with a proposal to update the EU ETS expected by July 2026. The review covers carbon removals, new sector inclusions, carbon leakage post-CBAM phase-out, and possible linking with other carbon markets.
events.analyst_note: Biggest structural uncertainty for EUA pricing beyond 2030. Scope of carbon removals inclusion and whether aviation free allocation phase-out timeline is hardened are the key variables to watch.

scenarios.rationale: The Commission likely delivers a balanced framework with moderate inclusion of carbon removals and selective sectoral expansions, though key decisions on aviation scope extension may be deferred pending CORSIA assessment outcomes.

Comprehensive scope expansion including extra-EEA aviation flights and smaller maritime vessels, coupled with accelerated carbon removal integration, could substantially tighten supply-demand dynamics in the carbon market.

Political resistance to further sectoral burden and industry competitiveness concerns may result in limited structural changes, potentially disappointing market expectations for supply tightening mechanisms.

events.title: EU-UK ETS formal linking negotiations
events.summary: Formal EU-UK ETS linking negotiations launched the week of 19 January 2026. EU Climate Commissioner Wopke Hoekstra confirmed both sides are aiming to conclude as soon as possible, with no specific timeline set. The EU Council unanimously backed the negotiating mandate in November 2025; the Commission is now authorised to negotiate. This row tracks the active negotiations phase; milestone rows (technical design, agreement in principle, ratification) will be added as dates are confirmed.
events.analyst_note: The single most structurally important medium-term event for UKA pricing. Convergence with EUA price is the implied outcome of a successful link — UKA currently trades at a material discount. Watch for technical design milestones and any public signals on timeline from either side.

scenarios.rationale: Negotiations likely progress gradually through 2026 with technical milestones achieved, though a final linking agreement will likely be completed by 2028, supporting UKA convergence toward EUA levels whilst maintaining some discount to account for remaining implementation risks.

Early achievement of key technical agreements and conclusion of negotiations in time for their next summit, expected mid-2026, would accelerate UKA convergence prospects and reduce discount substantially.

Technical complexities or political setbacks could delay progress beyond Q4 2026 expectations, given negotiations took nearly nine years for Swiss-EU linkage, potentially widening the UKA-EUA discount temporarily.

events.title: EU ETS annual surrender deadline (2025 emissions)
events.summary: 30 April 2026 is the annual deadline for EU ETS installations and aircraft operators to surrender allowances covering their 2025 verified emissions. A recurring compliance demand event that drives EUA buying pressure through Q1 each year.
events.analyst_note: Near-term bullish price dynamic. Any shortfall vs verified emissions amplifies spot buying. Monitor EU registry data on verified emissions vs outstanding positions into April.

scenarios.rationale: The annual surrender deadline appears likely to proceed smoothly with moderate demand, reflecting over 99% compliance achieved by shipping companies in previous deadlines and established market mechanisms.

Stronger-than-expected buying pressure could materialise if installations face shortfalls between verified emissions and surrendered allowances similar to the maritime sector's experience, potentially intensifying demand ahead of the deadline.

Limited price response might occur if companies have already secured sufficient allowances during the quarter or if substantial revenues of €38.8 billion generated in 2024 indicate ample liquidity dampening late procurement urgency.

events.title: COP31 — Belém, Brazil
events.summary: COP31 takes place in Belém, Brazil in November 2026. Article 6 rules remain not fully settled following COP29. COP31 is the next major deadline for operationalising the Paris Agreement's international carbon market mechanisms (Article 6.2 bilateral agreements and Article 6.4 centralised mechanism). Outcome has direct read-across to CORSIA-eligible credit demand and voluntary market integrity frameworks.
events.analyst_note: Article 6.4 supervisory body progress is the key variable — specifically whether the centralised mechanism begins issuing A6.4ERs at scale in time to influence the CORSIA-eligible supply pool. Bilateral Article 6.2 pipeline is already moving but quality and additionality of ITMOs remains contested. COP31 outcome will either accelerate or further delay the operationalisation timeline that VCM and CORSIA pricing depends on.

scenarios.rationale: COP31 will likely deliver incremental progress on Article 6.4 operational details and bilateral Article 6.2 frameworks without fundamentally altering the current implementation trajectory.
Accelerated Article 6.4 methodology approvals and enhanced bilateral cooperation frameworks could significantly expand the pipeline of CORSIA-eligible credits and high-integrity VCM supply.
Further delays in operationalising Article 6 mechanisms or restrictive integrity requirements could constrain credit supply whilst demand continues to grow across compliance and voluntary markets.

events.title: EU ETS Commission statutory review (July 2026)
events.summary: Distinct from the post-2030 proposal (REG-019). The Commission has a statutory obligation to report by end of July 2026 on: negative emissions accounting under EU ETS, feasibility of lowering the 20MW installation threshold, municipal waste incineration inclusion, CCU double-counting, and the functioning of aviation ETS and CORSIA.
events.analyst_note: Hard statutory deadline creates a defined catalyst. Waste incineration inclusion and negative emissions accounting are the variables with the most direct price read-across. CCU double-counting clarification could affect industrial sector compliance costs. Low probability of major structural surprise but watch for scope signals on waste and negative emissions.

scenarios.rationale: The Commission will likely deliver a measured assessment recommending the inclusion of municipal waste incineration from 2028 whilst maintaining conservative approaches to negative emissions accounting and CCU.

The statutory review could unveil broader scope expansion including full biogenic emissions coverage for waste incineration and accelerated negative emissions accounting, potentially boosting demand significantly.
The report might recommend delayed implementation or narrowed scope for waste incineration inclusion alongside conservative treatment of negative emissions, limiting near-term demand expansion.

events.title: CORSIA Phase 1 end and Phase 2 transition
events.summary: CORSIA mandatory Phase 1 (2024–2026) concludes at end of 2026, marking the first mandatory phase with real airline offsetting obligations for international emissions above the 2020 baseline. The scheme transitions to Phase 2 terms from 2027. Demand outlook through the end of Phase 1 is driven by a handful of major markets, and a supply crunch is emerging in CORSIA-eligible credits.
events.analyst_note: Transition from Phase 1 to Phase 2 introduces uncertainty around baseline recalculation and eligible unit criteria for the new phase. Supply crunch in CORSIA-eligible credits is already visible — the pool of qualifying project vintages is constrained relative to projected Phase 1 offsetting demand. Watch ICAO Technical Advisory Body outputs on Phase 2 methodology and any changes to eligible fuels criteria.

scenarios.rationale: The transition from Phase 1 to Phase 2 likely proceeds with moderate baseline adjustments whilst maintaining existing supply constraints, given the continued authorization bottlenecks and significant supply shortage during Phase I.

Substantial supply shortages materialise as CORSIA becomes mandatory for virtually all ICAO member states whilst LoA issuance remains limited due to ongoing regulatory developments, creating severe market tightness.

Baseline recalculation methodology proves more generous than expected and cumulative supply of CORSIA-eligible credits between 2028 and 2030 could reach 300 million tonnes as authorization processes accelerate, easing immediate demand pressures.

cards.headline: EUA Rout Deepens as Q1 Closes Ugly
cards.label: EUA Rout Deepens as Q1 Closes Ugly
cards.body: European carbon allowances extended their brutal decline, shedding 8.9% over the week and now sitting nearly 24% below levels from three months prior. The selloff reflects a confluence of bearish fundamentals including weak industrial demand, elevated renewable generation, and persistent natural gas softness reducing coal switching incentives. Speculative positioning has turned increasingly short as compliance buyers remain sidelined ahead of the April surrender deadline. The upcoming annual surrender for 2025 emissions in 31 days should theoretically provide support, but verified emissions data suggests ample hedged positions among obligated parties. The post-2030 consultation closing in May adds medium-term uncertainty, with stakeholders divided on Market Stability Reserve parameters and free allocation phase-out timelines. Technical signals remain mixed despite the directional move, with oversold indicators suggesting potential for a relief rally into compliance season. Institutional flows indicate continued rotation from EU carbon into other asset classes as macro headwinds persist across European industrial equities.
cards.source: CO2.L ETF data, EU ETS registry, ICE Endex futures

cards.headline: UK Floor Price Hike Looms in Days
cards.label: UK Floor Price Hike Looms in Days
cards.body: The UK ETS auction reserve price rises from £22 to £28 in nine days, representing a 27% increase in the effective price floor for British carbon allowances. UKA has declined 15.5% over three months, with spot prices at £34.55 now trading only marginally above the incoming floor threshold. This compression between market price and reserve creates asymmetric risk profiles; auctions clearing below reserve would be cancelled, tightening supply and forcing compliance buyers into secondary markets. The mechanism effectively establishes a harder put option under UKA prices than previously existed. Notably, the gap to EUA pricing has widened considerably given the sharper European selloff, with UK carbon now commanding a premium on a GBP-adjusted basis that reflects both policy divergence and thinner liquidity. From 2027, the ARP increases annually in line with a predetermined trajectory, embedding structural price support absent from the EU framework. Compliance entities should reassess hedging strategies given this imminent floor elevation.
cards.source: UK ETS Authority, BEIS policy documents, ICE UK Allowance futures

cards.headline: CORSIA Credits Outperform Carbon Complex Broadly
cards.label: CORSIA Credits Outperform Carbon Complex Broadly
cards.body: Aviation sector credits posted modest gains for the week and now show 12.3% appreciation over three months, making CORSIA the standout performer across tracked carbon instruments. The bullish signal contrasts sharply with weakness in compliance markets and reflects tightening eligibility criteria under ICAO's first compliance phase running through 2026. Airlines are increasingly securing forward volumes as the baseline adjustment from pandemic-era traffic normalizes offsetting obligations higher. Quality premiums within eligible credit categories have compressed as buyers accept broader vintage and project type exposure to meet growing demand. The voluntary carbon market reference price at $6.50 per tonne remains soft but showed weekly improvement, with CORSIA-eligible credits commanding meaningful premiums to generic VCM pricing. Notably, CORSIA credit supply remains constrained by stringent registry and methodology requirements that exclude significant VCM inventory. Airlines with concentrated route exposure to participating states face material procurement challenges into 2027 as compliance true-ups approach.
cards.source: ICAO CORSIA registry, S&P Global Platts, voluntary carbon indices
